title: AI: no casting into an empty graveyard
notes: The AI no longer casts graveyard-return spells with nothing to return. It now reads conditions like "permanent card with mana value 3 or less" (Sevinne's Reclamation) and only casts them when its own graveyard has a card that fits.

title: Sevinne's Reclamation; flashback fix
notes: Sevinne's Reclamation: cast with flashback, it copies itself, so you return two permanents with mana value 3 or less.

Flashback cards could also be cast from your graveyard for their normal mana cost, because the game misread flashback's reminder text. From the graveyard they're now castable only for their flashback cost (then exiled).

title: Goldspan Dragon
notes: Goldspan Dragon: it makes a Treasure when it becomes the target of a spell (yours or the AI's), not just when it attacks, and while it's out your Treasures tap for two mana.
"Whenever ~ becomes the target of a spell (or ability)" triggers work in general now.

title: Xorn and "plus an additional token" effects
notes: Xorn and Jolene, the Plunder Queen: whenever you'd create Treasures, you create one more. Worldwalker Helm adds a Map to artifact tokens, Tippy-Toe adds a Food to any tokens, and Chatterfang adds that many 1/1 Squirrels. These apply before Doubling Season and other doublers, so Xorn + Doubling Season turns 1 Treasure into 4.

title: Full layer system; the AI answers your triggers
notes: The AI can counter your triggered abilities. If it holds Stifle or another "counter target triggered ability" card and your trigger is worth stopping (big card draw, a pile of tokens, real damage, removal, an extra turn), it casts it. Small triggers like gaining 1 life are let through.

Types and colors (layers 4 and 5) now go by timestamp too. Effects that make something a creature, a Frog, a Mountain, an artifact or a color apply in the order they happened, and each one sees the result of the ones before it.

Board-wide layer effects: Humility, Dress Down, Opalescence, March of the Machines, Blood Moon (nonbasic lands become Mountains that tap for red), Mycosynth Lattice, Painter's Servant, Shifting Sky, Arcane Adaptation and Conspiracy. Humility + Opalescence follows the official ruling: whichever entered last decides whether Humility is a 4/4 or everything is 1/1.

Turn to Frog, Ovinize, Metamorphic Blast and "becomes [color]" change the creature's type, color and abilities, not just its P/T. Frogify, Kenrith's Transformation, Darksteel Mutation, Deep Freeze, Song of the Dryads and Imprisoned in the Moon work as Auras, and everything reverts when the Aura leaves.
A permanent that lost its abilities also loses its triggers, static effects and mana abilities, whichever effect took them away.

title: The stack, and rules layers
notes: Stack panel: the right-hand rail shows everything waiting to resolve (spells, abilities and triggers, yours in green and the AI's in red), with the next to resolve at the top.

The AI's triggered abilities now go on the stack. When one is about to resolve and you have an instant or flash card you can afford, the game pauses so you can respond, like it does for the AI's spells. Stifle and other "counter target triggered ability" cards work, including Spider-Sense, which now also counters sorceries. If you have nothing to respond with, it doesn't stop.

Rules layers: "loses all abilities" now goes by timestamp. Abilities granted afterwards (a spell, an Aura, an anthem that entered later) still apply, and ones from before don't. A creature that lost its abilities can't use its activated or mana abilities either.

Base power/toughness effects ("becomes a 4/4", "has base power and toughness 1/1", Auras that set P/T) apply in timestamp order, so the latest wins. Counters, pumps and anthems are added on top, and "switch power and toughness" (new) applies last.

title: Order your triggers; divide combat damage
notes: When several of your abilities trigger at the same time (one spell resolving, several creatures entering at once, combat damage…), you choose the order they resolve in. Identical triggers aren't asked about. Everything that triggered together now goes on the stack together: the active player's triggers first, so the other player's resolve first, as in the rules. Turn the prompt off with "Ask me to order my triggers" in the game menu (☰).

Combat damage: when your attacker is blocked by two or more creatures, or by one while it has trample, you divide its damage with +/− buttons. Any split among the blockers is allowed (the current rules have no damage assignment order). With trample, damage reaches the player only once every blocker has lethal damage (1 with deathtouch). "Default" fills in the usual lethal-to-each split.

title: Prepared copies use the stack; Chains and Underrealm Lich
notes: Prepared: casting a copy of a prepared creature's spell now puts it on the stack like any spell. The other player can respond to it or counter it (it's judged as the spell, so "counter target instant spell" works on a copied Seething Song). Countering the copy leaves the creature on the battlefield, unprepared. Checked against the real two-faced card data (Secrets of Strixhaven "prepare" cards).
Chains of Mephistopheles: a draw other than the first in a player's draw step becomes "discard a card, then draw", or a mill if their hand is empty.
Underrealm Lich: each of your draws becomes "look at the top three, put one into your hand and the rest into your graveyard".

title: Draw replacement effects
notes: Teferi's Ageless Insight and Alhammarret's Archive: every card you draw except the first one in your draw step becomes two. Thought Reflection doubles every draw. Several of these together multiply (Thought Reflection + Teferi's Ageless Insight draws 4 for 1).
Notion Thief: your opponent's draws (other than their first in the draw step) are skipped, and its controller draws instead.
Narset, Parter of Veils and Spirit of the Labyrinth stop draws after the first one each turn.
Laboratory Maniac and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries: drawing from an empty library wins the game instead of losing it.

title: Your Spider-Verse deck
notes: Prepared (Secrets of Strixhaven): Blazing Firesinger enters prepared; Joined Researchers, Lorehold Archivist and Harmonized Trio become prepared when their condition is met. While prepared, right-click the creature to cast a copy of its spell (pay its cost, at that spell's speed). Doing so unprepares it. The card shows a ✦ Prepared badge.

"From anywhere other than your hand" triggers work for lands too: Shadow of the Goblin, The Lost and the Damned and Ghost-Spider trigger when you play or put a land onto the battlefield from exile. Advanced Reconstruction's level 3 discount applies to those spells.

Spider-Verse copies only once each turn, and copies of permanent spells have haste. The Twelfth Doctor gives your first spell each turn from outside your hand demonstrate (you copy it, then the opponent copies it) and grows whenever you copy a spell.

The War Doctor gets time counters when other cards are exiled, deals damage equal to its time counters when it attacks, and exiles a creature killed that way. Laelia grows when cards are exiled from your library or graveyard.

The Tenth Doctor suspends the card it exiles with three time counters, and its {7} ability time travels three times (add or remove counters; a suspended card whose last counter is removed is cast for free). The Eleventh Doctor suspends a card from your hand.

Fixed: Hex Magic, Heroes' Hangout (only the chosen card is playable), Dance with Calamity (exile as many as you like, then cast them free if the total is 13 or less), Rousing Refrain (exiles itself with three time counters), Daredevil (+2/+1 when the card is a Hero), Cait Sith (+X/+0 equal to the card's mana value), Chaos Channeler and Wand of Wonder (d20 results), Zuko (Firebending adds {R}{R}{R} on attack), Jem Lightfoote, Shadow of the Goblin (discard, then draw), Advanced Reconstruction, Ember Island Production (the copy is a 4/4 Hero or 2/2 Coward), Spider-Man No More (a 1/1 Citizen with only defender), Interdimensional Web Watch (its mana only casts spells from exile), and Lotus Bloom and Ancestral Vision (can only be suspended, not cast for nothing).

title: Rooms, Hideaway, Gwen Stacy and more
notes: Rooms work. Cast either door and that door enters unlocked, with its "When you unlock this door" ability triggering. Right-click the Room to unlock the other door by paying its mana cost as a sorcery; this doesn't use the stack. Only unlocked doors' abilities apply, and the card shows a 🔓/🔒 badge for each door. The AI unlocks its doors too.

Hideaway: the hidden card is no longer free to cast at any time. It's played only when the card says so (Windbrisk Heights after three attackers, Mosswort Bridge at 10 power, Howltooth Hollow with empty hands…), and you can play it as your land if it's a land. You can see your hidden card; the opponent can't. Watcher for Tomorrow returns its card when it leaves, and Evercoat Ursine plays its cards on combat damage.

Gwen Stacy: the exiled card stays playable for as long as you control her, not just that turn. Ghost-Spider gets its +1/+1 counter when you cast a spell or play a land from exile, and its "Remove two counters" ability takes any counters and can't be used without them.
Spinneret and Spiderling: its counter needs two or more attacking Spiders, and "deals 4 or more damage" exiles a card you can play until the end of your next turn.
Superior Foes of Spider-Man: triggers only on spells with mana value 4 or more, and the exiled card stays playable until it exiles the next one.
Franklin Richards, Ascendant: discovers 6 at the beginning of combat if you've cast a noncreature spell this turn.
Split and modal double-faced cards name both halves when you choose which one to cast.

title: "Its controller" after a stolen creature leaves
notes: Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Generous Gift and other "its controller gets…" removal now reward the player who controlled the creature, not its owner. Exiling a creature you'd stolen gives you the basic land (or life, or Elephant). Before, the creature had already gone back to its owner by the time the effect asked, so the opponent got it. Works for stolen tokens too.

title: Spree, signets, Grenzo and land drops
notes: Spree cards work. You choose which extra costs to pay when you cast, pay the base cost plus each one, and each chosen mode happens. Before, the modes were never offered, so the spell cost only its base and the effect had to be applied by hand. All 21 Spree cards are covered (Insatiable Avarice, Final Showdown, Trash the Town, Metamorphic Blast, Smuggler's Surprise…).

Signets chain properly. A land can pay for one signet and that signet's mana can pay for the next, so a basic plus two signets makes 3 mana. Before, the game said you couldn't afford spells you could.
Grenzo, Dungeon Warden: its {2} ability works. It puts the bottom card of your library into your graveyard, and onto the battlefield if it's a creature with power no greater than Grenzo's.

Lands from exile (and from hand) now respect your land drops in the normal mode. Once you've played your land for the turn, you can't play another unless something like Explore allows it. The "Play it anyway" button is gone.

"It gains [ability] until end of turn" (Final Showdown, and many other cards) now gives the real ability for the turn. Before, it could be stored as a permanent ability under the wrong name and not work at all.

New effects: a creature becoming a 0/1 (or similar) with base power and toughness until end of turn; a creature gaining a quoted triggered ability until end of turn; "Choose a creature you control" (not targeted).

title: Black Widow, Super Spy fixed
notes: Black Widow, Super Spy: when she deals combat damage to a player, they exile until a nonland card and you choose: put a +1/+1 counter on her, or skip the counter and cast the exiled card this turn using mana of any type. Before, choosing no counter did nothing; you never got the card.

title: Plargg and Nassari fixed
notes: Plargg and Nassari: the upkeep trigger now works with the card's real wording. Each player exiles until a nonland card, your opponent picks one you can't have, and you may cast the other for free. Before, the card's text wasn't recognised, so you never got to cast anything.
Under the hood: "cast it for free" effects that run during triggers are now always connected to the casting code.

title: Treasures pay for spells again
notes: Treasures made by cards (the ones with real token art) read "Sacrifice this token", and the game only understood "Sacrifice this artifact", so it didn't see them as mana at all: no auto-sacrifice, no paying with them, and the AI couldn't use its Treasures either. They now count as mana everywhere, and the "Auto-sacrifice Treasures" setting works with them.
Same fix for other sacrifice-for-mana tokens and permanents worded "this token" or "this permanent" (Gold, Lotus Petal-style tokens…).

title: See what was chosen
notes: Permanents that make a choice as they enter now show it on the card: the color for Thriving lands (and Utopia Sprawl, Caged Sun…), the creature type for Cavern of Souls and similar cards, the card type for Serra's Emissary, and the mode for Sieges. Hover the badge for details.
Two copies with different choices (say, a red and a blue Thriving Bluff) no longer stack together on the battlefield.

title: Windfall fixed
notes: Windfall: each player discards their hand, then every player draws as many cards as the most anyone discarded. Before, only you drew, and you drew 0.

title: Tapping shows right away
notes: When you activate an ability with {T} in its cost (Chaos Wand, Currency Converter…), the permanent is shown tapped (and your mana spent) as soon as you pay. Before, the board only updated after the ability had finished, so it looked untapped while you made its choices.

"Cast a spell from among them for free" choices (Chaos Wand, Etali, Crabomination…) no longer have a "Cancel spell" button that undid the whole ability. Choose none to skip the spell. Backing out of the free spell's own target also just skips that spell.

title: Extra land drops
notes: Explore and other "you may play an additional land this turn" spells no longer ask "Yes/No" when they resolve. They just give you the extra land drop, and the limit still applies afterwards. "Two/three additional lands" (Summer Bloom and friends) now count correctly too.

title: Thriving lands ask for a color
notes: Thriving lands now ask you to choose a color when they enter, with your card data's current wording, where "enters tapped" and "As it enters, choose a color" are on the same line. Before, that wording was missed, so you were never asked. The same fix applies to other "As it enters, choose a creature type / card type" cards.

title: Author of Shadows (really)
notes: Author of Shadows works with its current Oracle wording ("exile all opponents' graveyards"). It exiles their graveyard, lets you choose a nonland card, and that card is castable from your "From exile" panel for as long as it stays exiled, with mana of any type. Its steps also work one at a time, so small wording differences in card data no longer stop the whole ability.

title: AI respects deathtouch
notes: The AI's combat planning now sees deathtouch (and other keywords) that only apply while attacking, such as "Attacking creatures you control have deathtouch". Before, it could block a 1/1 that had deathtouch this way with a big creature. It also judges its own attacks and your counterattacks with these keywords in mind.
Keyword counters (a deathtouch, flying, lifelink, trample… counter) now give the creature that keyword. Before, they did nothing, and the AI didn't know about them either.

title: Author of Shadows enters trigger
notes: Author of Shadows' enters ability now goes off whichever wording your card data uses ("all opponents' graveyards" or "each opponent's graveyard", "that card" or "it", "any color" or "any type"). It exiles the graveyard and lets you choose the nonland card to cast.

title: Author of Shadows
notes: Author of Shadows works with the card's current wording ("mana of any type"). Before, that wording wasn't recognized, so the exile-and-cast ability did nothing. The other theft cards (Black Cat, Tinybones, Laughing Jasper Flint, Shadow of the Enemy, Rakdos, Breeches, Gonti…) now accept both "any color" and "any type" wordings too.

title: Zara, Renegade Recruiter
notes: Zara, Renegade Recruiter: when you attack with her, the log now lists the AI's whole hand (it used to just say she looked), then you choose a creature to put in attacking. The stolen-card popup no longer shows the card sideways.

title: Escape to the Wilds
notes: Escape to the Wilds now lets you play the five exiled cards, lands included, until the end of your next turn. They show in your "From exile" panel. Before, it exiled them and you had to apply the rest by hand. Other "you may play cards exiled this way" effects work too.

title: See who blocks whom
notes: Combat now draws a dashed blue line from each blocker to the attacker it blocks. The blocker end has a dot, the attacker end a red ring, and the middle has the attacker's number. Lines appear as blocks are declared and disappear when combat ends.

title: Vengeful Regrowth
notes: Vengeful Regrowth now makes a 4/2 green Plant Warrior with reach for each land it returns. Before, it returned the lands but made no tokens. This also fixes other "return cards from your graveyard… then do something that many times" effects.

title: Thriving lands
notes: Thriving lands (Thriving Bluff, Moor, Heath, Isle, Grove) now ask you to choose a color as they enter, leaving out their own color, and then tap for either their own color or the chosen one. Before, they only ever made their own color, so the choice did nothing.

title: Treasure auto-pay setting
notes: New setting: "Auto-sacrifice Treasures to pay", on the setup screen and in the in-game menu. When it's on (the default), auto-pay uses Treasures after your lands and other mana, as before. When it's off, auto-pay won't touch your Treasures: if your other mana can't cover a cost, you're asked whether to sacrifice them. This also covers other sacrifice-for-mana permanents such as Lotus Petal.

title: Full update log
notes: New: a full update log with every version's notes and a search box, so you can type a card name to find its fix. Open it from "Full update log" next to the version number on the setup screen, from the in-game menu (☰ → Update log), or from the button on the what's-new popup.

title: Theft deck: the last details
notes: Ian Malcolm, Chaotician: each player can cast only one spell per turn from the cards exiled with him, only on their own turn and only while he's on the battlefield.

Don Andres makes creatures you control but don't own Pirates, and Laughing Jasper Flint makes them Mercenaries, so they count for Pirate and outlaw cards such as Breeches, Ramirez and Laughing Jasper Flint.
Cards the AI exiles face down (Expensive Taste, Gonti, Black Cat) stay hidden from you until it plays them. Cards you exile that way stay visible to you.

title: Theft deck overhaul
notes: Cards that let you play your opponent's cards now work. Exiled cards you may play show in your "From exile" panel and can be cast from the right-click menu. Where the card says so, you can pay with mana of any color, and the permission lasts "this turn" or "for as long as it remains exiled" as written.

Newly working: Expensive Taste, Black Cat, Cunning Thief, Author of Shadows, Crabomination, Breach the Multiverse, Brainstealer Dragon, Overture (Jidoor), Tinybones, the Pickpocket, Tinybones, Bauble Burglar, The Horus Heresy, Kefka, Dancing Mad, Fevered Suspicion, Plargg and Nassari, Nathan Drake, Laughing Jasper Flint, Lethal Scheme's connive, Locke, Treasure Hunter, Extract Brain, Etali, Primal Storm, Shadow of the Enemy, Zara, Renegade Recruiter, Rakdos, the Muscle, Ramirez DePietro, Dream Harvest, Breeches, Brazen Plunderer, Gríma, Saruman's Footman, Gonti, Night Minister, Don Andres, the Renegade, Intellect Devourer, Hostage Taker (any-color mana, cast it any time while exiled), Chaos Wand, Strago and Relm, Wand of Wonder, Ian Malcolm, Bident of Thassa, Black Market Connections, J. Jonah Jameson, Labyrinth Raptor, Grenzo's second mode and Port Razer's extra combat.
Fixed: "instant or sorcery card" targets could pick creature cards, for example Dire Fleet Daredevil.
Fixed: modal choices with mode names ("Sell Contraband — …") only did part of each mode.

title: Stolen-card popup and King Narfi's Betrayal
notes: When a card changes hands (Jhoira, Control Magic, Hostage Taker, casting an opponent's exiled card…), a popup now shows the card and says who took it from where.

King Narfi's Betrayal works. Chapter I mills four from each player and lets you exile a creature or planeswalker card from each graveyard. Chapters II and III let you cast those cards that turn, spending mana as though it were any color. The AI can cast your exiled cards too, and your own exile panel lists the ones you can cast.

title: AI uses Currency Converter
notes: The AI now uses Currency Converter's {T} ability to turn its exiled cards into Treasures and Rogues. Before, it only ever used the loot ability, and it skips the {T} ability when nothing has been exiled with the Converter.

title: Cryptbreaker
notes: Cryptbreaker's second ability now taps three untapped Zombies you control as its cost, and Cryptbreaker can be one of them even the turn it arrives. Before, it tapped nothing and worked with fewer than three Zombies. It also now makes you lose 1 life when you draw. Other abilities with a "Tap N untapped … you control" cost work the same way.

title: Smarter AI targeting
notes: The AI no longer casts removal like Despark when nothing is a legal target. It now checks target limits such as "with mana value 4 or greater" or "with power 3 or less" before casting, and its removal scoring respects them too.

title: Brainstorm, Brainsurge and surveil
notes: Fixed: Brainstorm, Brainsurge and similar spells let you pick the spell itself to put back, because the game still counted it as being in your hand while it resolved. A spell on the stack no longer counts as in your hand for any effect. This also fixes discards, "cards in your hand" counts and "shuffle your hand into your library" effects that could include the spell.
Brainstorm-style choices now show the cards you just drew first, and say which card ends up on top.
Surveil now offers only Top or Graveyard, as the rules say. It no longer offers Bottom.
Fixed a hidden crash risk in a few "cast it without paying its mana cost" effects.

title: Omnath, Locus of the Void and Proteus Staff
notes: Omnath, Locus of the Void works. It gets +1/+1 for each unspent mana you have, and your unspent mana turns colorless instead of emptying between steps. "Players don't lose unspent mana" (Upwelling) and other "becomes colorless instead" cards now work too.

Proteus Staff works. It puts the target creature on the bottom of its owner's library, and its controller reveals cards from the top until a creature card, puts that onto the battlefield and the rest on the bottom. Before, it did nothing.

title: Blocked stays blocked
notes: A creature that was blocked stays blocked even if all its blockers are removed before combat damage. It deals no damage unless it has trample, in which case all its damage goes to the player. Ninjutsu also can't return it as unblocked. Before, it was treated as unblocked and hit the player.

title: Serra's Emissary
notes: Serra's Emissary works: as it enters you choose a card type, and you and your creatures get protection from it. Your creatures can't be blocked, damaged or targeted by things of that type, and you can't be damaged or targeted by them either (for example, creatures can't deal combat damage to you). The AI usually picks creature.
"You have protection from …" now works on players in general.

title: Currency Converter and Nissa, Leyline Tamer
notes: Currency Converter works: when you discard a card you can exile it with the Converter, and its {T} ability puts one of those cards into your graveyard and makes a Treasure (land) or a 2/2 black Rogue (nonland). Before, the discard trigger exiled a random card from your graveyard and the {T} ability did nothing.

Nissa, Leyline Tamer only puts a creature onto the battlefield the first time her landfall ability resolves each turn. Before, later landfalls that turn put the top revealed card onto the battlefield even when it wasn't a creature.

title: Ginger, Queen of Sweets
notes: Ginger, Queen of Sweets now makes real Gingerbrute tokens: 1/1 haste Food Golems that can sacrifice for 3 life. Before, it made a blank 1/1 token because the game mistook the "Ginger" in "Gingerbrute" for the card's own name. This also fixes other cards whose name is the start of a longer word in their text.
"Can't be blocked this turn except by creatures with haste" (and similar) now lets those creatures block. Before, it made the attacker fully unblockable.

title: Sephara and alternative costs
notes: Sephara, Sky's Blade now gives your other flying creatures indestructible.

Sephara can be cast for {W} by tapping four untapped flying creatures. Spells with a "You may … rather than pay this spell's mana cost" alternative cost now offer it when you can pay it. This also covers Force of Will-style "exile a card from your hand" costs.

title: Occult Epiphany
notes: Occult Epiphany now makes a 1/1 flying Spirit for each card type among the cards you discarded. Before, it made none. When the AI casts it, it tries to discard a mix of card types.

title: Unlimited mulligans and card fixes
notes: New setup option: Unlimited free mulligans. Mulligan as often as you like and always keep seven. It only affects you, not the AI.
Fixed a broad bug with optional triggers like "you may discard a card. If you do, draw two cards": the "if you do" part never happened. This fixes Bitter Reunion and many similar cards.
"You may play those cards" effects now let you play lands too, not just cast spells (Atsushi, the Blazing Sky and other impulse draws).
Power and toughness that depend on a count (Uurg, Spawn of Turg and other legends whose text uses their short name) now update as the count changes.
Captain America, Team Leader now puts +1/+1 counters on the entering Hero and on himself.
Folk Hero gives your commander its card-draw trigger.
Breaching Dragonstorm no longer moves the spell it cast into your hand, and puts spells over mana value 8 into your hand instead of casting them.
Herald's Horn shows you the top card when it isn't a match, and logs the reveal when it is.
Myriad Landscape's two lands now have to share a land type.
Maestros Theater and other "sacrifice it. When you do, …" lands now fetch their land.
Exemplar of Light draws a card the first time each turn you put +1/+1 counters on it.
Righteous Valkyrie's +2/+2 applies when you have at least 7 more life than you started with.
Horizon Explorer makes your lands enter untapped.
Cursed Mirror can become a copy of a creature with haste until end of turn.

title: Jace, Thassa's Oracle and the precon gaps
notes: Jace, the Mind Sculptor works: +2 looks at the top card of a player's library and can put it on the bottom, 0 draws three and puts two back, −1 bounces a creature, and −12 exiles a player's library and shuffles their hand into it. The AI uses all four abilities.
Thassa's Oracle now wins the game when your devotion to blue is at least the number of cards left in your library. Before, it only put a card into your hand.

The three new precons now run almost entirely automatically. Newly working: Fact or Fiction, Mass Polymorph, Synthetic Destiny, Teferi's Reproach, Hoarder's Greed, Jhoira, Weatherlight Corsair, Dack Fayden, Helping Hand, Scarlet Witch, Heroic Sacrifice, Eventide's Shadow, Aberrant Return, Arcane Denial's delayed draws, The Ur-Sphinx, Nissa, Leyline Tamer, Oft-Nabbed Goat, Gift of Immortality and Love on the Battlefield.

Avengers triggers now work: Captain America, Living Legend untaps your creatures the first time they tap on your turn. Captain Marvel copies counters you put on your other creatures. She-Hulk adds counters when a Hero is blocked. Hercules grows when he's dealt damage. Shang-Chi's tenth counter draws five cards. Jocasta grows from commander damage and returns from your graveyard when your commander attacks. Falcon and Redwing makes Birds. Iron Man and War Machine buff modified creatures. Vision, Hawkeye, Black Widow, Photon, Tamiyo, Kindred Discovery, Massacre Girl, Lasting Tarfire and Niv-Mizzet, Ghost Counsel also work.

Three Avengers cards printed under Marvel names now load as the cards they reprint: Raise Repulsor Shields as Raise the Palisade, Avengers Monitoring Station as Herald's Horn, and S.H.I.E.L.D. Spy Satellite as Fellwar Stone.
Fixed: casting Dismantling Wave (or any spell with a "When you cycle" ability) also ran its cycling ability.
A trigger with no legal targets now says so in the log instead of asking you to apply it by hand.

title: Three new precons
notes: New precons under Precon: Multiverse Reforged (Jace, Multiverse Architect, from Reality Fracture Commander), Blight Curse (Auntie Ool, Cursewretch, from Lorwyn Eclipsed Commander) and Avengers Assemble (Captain America, Team Leader, from Marvel Super Heroes Commander). About 87% of their cards work fully automatically so far, and the rest show up in the log so you can apply them by hand.

title: Smarter AI planeswalkers
notes: The AI skips any planeswalker ability the game can't carry out fully. Before, it sometimes picked an ability that only got logged as "apply by hand" and lost the loyalty for nothing (Saheeli, Sublime Artificer's −2, for example). It also won't use a −X tutor when there's nothing in its library to find.

Now working: Ajani Steadfast's −2 (+1/+1 counter on each of your creatures and a loyalty counter on each other planeswalker), Tezzeret the Seeker's −X (an artifact with mana value X or less onto the battlefield), and Chandra, Torch of Defiance's +1 (cast the exiled card, or she deals 2 damage to each opponent).
Fixed "If you don't, …" sentences, which were being cut off partway.

title: Sen Triplets works against you too
notes: When the AI's Sen Triplets (or any "you may cast spells from that player's hand this turn" card) targets you, the AI plays your lands and casts your spells with its own mana, and controls what it casts. You can't cast spells or activate abilities that turn. The log says "from your hand" when it does this.

title: Mindslaver and Sen Triplets
notes: Mindslaver, Worst Fears and Emrakul, the Promised End let you control the AI's next turn. During that turn you see the AI's hand, and each main phase a box lists everything the AI can do: play a land, cast a spell, use an ability or planeswalker. You pick, and its mana is tapped for it. In combat you choose which of its creatures attack and what they attack. Every choice its cards ask for (targets, modes, "may" questions, scry) comes to you. You still block with your own creatures as usual. After Emrakul's controlled turn, the AI takes an extra turn.

Sen Triplets: at your upkeep the AI can't cast spells or activate abilities that turn, and its hand is shown face up. You can double-click its cards to play its lands and cast its spells with your own mana, and you control whatever you cast. The same works for any "you may cast spells from that player's hand this turn" card.
If the AI uses one of these on you, the turn plays normally and the log tells you to play it as the AI would. The AI can't take over your turn yet.

title: "Built-in decks"
notes: The decks that come with the app are now listed under "Built-in decks".

title: "Claude decks"
notes: The "Sample" tab for the built-in decks is now called "Claude decks".

title: Deck links removed
notes: The "Deck link" option is gone. Moxfield blocks the app from reading its decks, so links weren't reliable. To bring in a deck from Moxfield or Archidekt, use Export there, copy the list as text, and paste it under "Paste list". That's now the default tab. If you paste a link into that box, the game tells you what to do instead.

title: Choose: mana creatures before or after lands
notes: New setting, "Auto-tap mana creatures": After lands (the default, so they can still attack or block) or Before lands (keep your lands untapped). It's on the setup screen and in the ☰ menu during a game, and it's remembered for next time. The other cards in your hand still come first: if tapping a mana creature would leave another spell uncastable, auto-tap won't do it. This setting only changes your own auto-tapping.

title: Smarter auto-tapping
notes: Auto-tapping looks at the other cards in your hand and your commander. If the cheapest way to pay would leave one of them uncastable when you could have afforded both, it taps different lands so you can still cast the other card. In random tests, the old auto-tapper stranded a castable card about 1 time in 20, and the new one didn't strand any. The AI pays the same way.

title: Respond to the AI's activated abilities
notes: When the AI activates an ability (anything except a mana ability), you can respond, the same as with its spells. The box says "AI is activating an ability", shows the ability's text, and says what it's targeting. The target glows red. Cast instants or use abilities in response, then let it resolve.
A counterspell that only counters spells can't counter an ability. Cards that say "counter target activated ability" can.
If "Let me respond to AI spells" is turned off, AI abilities resolve right away without pausing.

title: Commander damage from an animated Background
notes: If a Background (or any noncreature commander) becomes a creature and deals combat damage, it now gets its own commander-damage counter under the player's life total. The damage was always tracked and counted toward 21, but the counter only showed up for creature commanders.

title: "Another target"
notes: "Tap target permanent, then untap another target permanent" (Ral Zarek's +1) and similar abilities can't pick the same permanent twice. The second choice leaves out what you already picked.

title: Planeswalkers at sorcery speed
notes: Loyalty abilities follow the timing rule again: only on your own turn, in a main phase, with nothing on the stack. The exceptions still work: Teferi's Talent, Teferi, Temporal Archmage's emblem, Jace's Machinations, and anything else that says you may activate them on any player's turn.

title: Panharmonicon and other trigger doublers
notes: Panharmonicon works. When an artifact or creature enters, triggered abilities of your permanents trigger an additional time. That includes the entering card's own abilities and things like Soul Warden. Lands entering don't count, so landfall isn't doubled. Yarok, the Desecrated and Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines double every permanent entering. Teysa Karlov and Drivnod double "dies" triggers, such as Blood Artist.

title: Planar Incision
notes: Planar Incision (and any "exile it, then return it … with a +1/+1 counter on it" card) puts the counter on the creature when it comes back.
When the AI casts one of these exile-and-return spells, it aims it at its own creatures, not yours.

title: Sphinx of the Second Sun
notes: Sphinx of the Second Sun gives you an extra beginning phase after your second main phase. You untap, your upkeep triggers happen again, and you draw a card. Then the turn goes to the end step. This works for you and the AI. If you click Pass turn from your first main phase or combat, your second main phase still happens, so "at the beginning of your postcombat main phase" abilities still trigger.

title: Treasures from different cards stack together
notes: Treasure, Clue, Food, Blood, Map and other standard tokens are treated as the same token no matter which card made them. Before, Treasures from different cards were separate kinds of token. They showed up as separate piles and could count differently. Now they stack into one pile and use the real token art when it's available.

title: Blood Money
notes: Blood Money creates a tapped Treasure for each nontoken creature it destroys. Any "for each creature destroyed this way, …" card now works.

title: Tomb of Horrors Adventurer
notes: Tomb of Horrors Adventurer copies your second spell each turn twice once you've completed a dungeon. Before, it did nothing in that case.
Copying a creature or other permanent spell makes a token copy of it, so Tomb of Horrors Adventurer and other "copy that spell" effects now work on permanent spells. Before, those copies did nothing.
"Copy it twice" and "copy it three times" work.

title: Displacer Beast, ability words, landwalk AI
notes: Activated abilities with an ability word in front of them now work, like Displacer Beast's "Displacement — {3}{U}: Return this to its owner's hand". Before, the game didn't see them at all.

The AI knows islandwalk, swampwalk, forestwalk, mountainwalk and plainswalk make a creature unblockable when you control that land type, and plans its attacks with that in mind. Blocking rules for fear, intimidate, shadow, horsemanship, skulk and landwalk were checked and already worked.

title: See what the AI's spell is targeting
notes: When the AI casts a spell and you get the chance to respond, the box now says what it's targeting ("Targeting: your Serra Angel", "Targeting: you"), and the targeted card glows red on the battlefield. The AI picks its targets as it casts, the way the rules work, so the spell hits what was shown. If you remove or protect that target in response, it picks again.

title: Legends called by their first name; Ureni
notes: Legendary cards whose text uses just their first name now work, like "Whenever Ureni enters or attacks" or "Whenever Thrakkus attacks". Before, the game didn't recognize the short name, so those abilities never triggered. This affects many legends named "X of the Y" or "X the Y".
Ureni of the Unwritten puts the Dragon it finds onto the battlefield (it used to go to your hand). Any "look at the top N … put a card from among them onto the battlefield" works the same way.

title: Card sweep: auras, Craterhoof, ramp auras, triggers
notes: Auras grant their keywords reliably. An Aura that says "has flying, haste, and …", "gets +2/+2, has flying, and is an Angel", "has base power and toughness 8/8 and has trample", or gives a quoted ability ("has haste and '{T}, Discard a card: Draw a card'") now works. Before, many of these gave nothing. Auras like Runes of the Deus ("as long as enchanted creature is red…") check the creature's color or type as you play.
Craterhoof Behemoth gives +X/+X and trample. Before, it did nothing.
Utopia Sprawl, Wild Growth, Fertile Ground and Wolfwillow Haven make the extra mana when you tap the enchanted land. Cards that say "As this enters, choose a color" ask you for one.

New triggers: "Whenever an Angel / a Dragon / another Cat you control dies or attacks", "Whenever your commander attacks" (We Ride at Dawn, Tome of Legends, Norn's Choirmaster), "Whenever you gain life for the first time each turn" (Vanguard Seraph), "Whenever you cast an Aura" (Sram).
"Put a +1/+1 counter on it and it can't be blocked this turn" (Kappa Cannoneer) does both parts.

Completing a dungeon always counts, even if you back out of the last room's ability, so Safana's three Treasures work. When you're not in a dungeon, the right-hand column shows how many dungeons you've completed.

title: Venturing fixed
notes: Venturing and taking the initiative now move you exactly one room each time. The game used to read each dungeon's rooms from the card's text on Scryfall, and when that text didn't come through as expected, the dungeon could finish all at once. All four dungeons (Lost Mine of Phandelver, Dungeon of the Mad Mage, Tomb of Annihilation and Undercity) are now built into the game, room by room, so they always work the same way. The dungeon map now stays on screen while you're in a dungeon.

title: Contagion Engine, Dungeon Delver
notes: Contagion Engine: its enters-the-battlefield ability puts a -1/-1 counter only on the creatures of the player you target (before, it hit every creature, yours too). Its activated ability proliferates twice instead of once. The AI now uses proliferate abilities when that helps it. The same fixes apply to every "each creature target player controls" and "proliferate twice" card.
Dungeon Delver: while a commander creature you own is on the battlefield, each room ability triggers an additional time. Hama Pashar's "room abilities trigger an additional time" works too.
The dungeon map shows even if an older copy of the page is still loaded.

title: Silent Hallcreeper
notes: Silent Hallcreeper picks one mode each time it deals combat damage to a player, instead of doing all three at once. A mode it has already used isn't offered again. Once it becomes a copy of another creature, it no longer has the trigger. Any "choose one that hasn't been chosen" card works the same way.

title: Dungeon map moved
notes: The dungeon map now sits at the bottom of the right-hand column, under the game log. The card preview at the top keeps its full space. The map is also more compact.

title: Dungeon map; Yuan-Ti Malison
notes: Dungeon progress is shown on the right side of the screen, above the game log. You see a map of your dungeon and the AI's: rooms already visited are ticked, the current room is highlighted, and the rooms you can go to next are outlined. Hover a room to read it, or click the map to see every room in full.

Yuan-Ti Malison can't be blocked when it attacks alone, but can be blocked if anything attacks with it. The AI no longer treats it as always unblockable. The same check now covers "can't be blocked as long as you're the monarch" and "as long as you have the initiative."

title: Shark Typhoon sizes; AI uses The Chain Veil
notes: Shark Typhoon's Sharks are the right size. The real Shark token art has a printed 0/0, and the game was using that printed size instead of X. Sharks now come out X/X, both when you cycle it and when you cast a noncreature spell. The same fix covers any token made as "an X/X …" or "a 4/4 …" whose printed token says something else.

The Chain Veil: the AI now uses it. Once its planeswalkers have activated, it pays {4} and activates each one again, and it saves mana for this before casting spells. It also uses Oath of Teferi's second activation, which it used to skip. For you, the Veil already worked: each planeswalker gets another activation and its badge lights up again. You lose 2 life at your end step if you didn't activate any loyalty ability that turn.

title: Surveil fixes; commander zone choice
notes: The AI actually surveils and scries now — before, it always left every card on top. It bins lands it doesn't need and cards it can use from the graveyard, and keeps what it can cast soon. It also feeds Uurg and other graveyard payoffs.
"Whenever you scry or surveil" (Matoya, Proft and others) now triggers on surveil too, not just scry.

Enhanced Surveillance's extra cards work, "if you put a … card into your graveyard this way, put it into your hand" works (Chandra, Chill of Compliance), and "if you've scried or surveilled this turn" is checked.

Your commander no longer goes straight to the command zone. When it goes to your graveyard or exile, or gets bounced or tucked, a box by your life total asks: Command zone, or leave it there. If you'd rather it always go back automatically, change "Commander leaving play" in settings or the ☰ menu. The AI's commander still returns on its own.

title: Much faster with big boards; Rowan's emblem
notes: Big boards no longer lag. Drawing the screen with ~300 permanents went from ~140 ms to ~20 ms, the AI's attack planning with dozens of tokens is many times faster (it treats a pile of identical tokens as one kind of attacker), and checking what triggers after each event no longer slows down as the board grows. An AI turn on a 60-creature-per-side board went from minutes to a few seconds.

Rowan Kenrith's −8 emblem works: every ability you activate that isn't a mana ability — including loyalty abilities — is copied. The AI gives the emblem to itself. Locus of Enlightenment copies the same way.
"Target player gets an emblem" lets you choose who gets it.

title: From-exile zone
notes: New "From exile" box under each player's piles shows every card that can be cast from exile, tagged by why: Foretold, Plotted, Adventure, This turn / Until next turn (impulse draws), Free, Warp, and Suspend ⏳N (shown dimmed until it's castable).
Double-click a card there to cast it (or right-click for the options). Cards that can't be cast yet — foretold or plotted this turn, still suspended — are dimmed.
The AI's foretold cards show face down there and on its exile pile.

title: Planeswalker indicator on opponents' turns
notes: When you can use loyalty abilities on other players' turns — the emblem from Teferi's Talent or Teferi, Temporal Archmage, or Jace's Machinations for your Jaces that turn — your planeswalkers show the ⚡ ready / ✓ used tag on the AI's turn too. Without one of those, the tag only shows on your own turn.

title: Shark Typhoon
notes: Shark Typhoon's Shark counts X on the spell you cast: Blaze with X=4 makes a 5/5 (it was using the printed mana value, so X spells made tiny Sharks). Split cards use the half you cast.
Checked: noncreature spells only, the Shark has flying, and cycling makes an X/X Shark for the X you paid.

title: Dusk // Dawn
notes: Dawn (and other "return all creature cards with power 2 or less / mana value 3 or less from your graveyard" effects) only returns the creatures that fit — it was bringing back everything.
Dusk checked: destroys only creatures with power 3 or greater; Dawn is cast from the graveyard with aftermath and exiled afterwards.
The AI judges Dusk-style partial wipes by what they actually destroy on each side, instead of treating them like a full board wipe.

title: Waterbend, exhaust, convoke
notes: Waterbend works: when paying a waterbend cost, your untapped artifacts and creatures can each pay {1} of it (they're tapped after lands and rocks, and only for the waterbend part). Covers "As an additional cost, waterbend {N}" spells (Water Whip, Benevolent River Spirit), optional ones (Katara, Seeking Revenge asks), waterbend {X} (Waterbender's Restoration), Waterbend {N}: abilities (Katara, Water Tribe Rallier, Watery Grasp, Waterbender Ascension), Waterbending Lesson's "unless you waterbend {2}" and Ward—Waterbend.
Exhaust abilities ("Exhaust — {4}: …", Aetherdrift and Avatar cards like Bitter Work, Boom Scholar, Invasion Submersible) were missing from the ability menu — they're back, usable once per game.
Convoke checked: creatures pay for {1} or a mana of their color, and the auto-payer uses lands first.
Also fixed: "if it has N or more quest counters on it" (Waterbender Ascension) and "if ~ is tapped" (Katara, Bending Prodigy).

title: Board grouping and attack tax display
notes: Mana rocks (Sol Ring, Signets, Talismans, Mind Stone…) now sit with your lands, after a divider, instead of mixing with your other permanents.

Rows are sorted and grouped: commanders first, then creature cards, then tokens; planeswalkers first among other permanents, then enchantments, then artifacts; basic lands by type, then nonbasics. Thin dividers separate the groups.
The prompt bar in the middle (declare attackers, targeting, the AI's spell) no longer covers your front row — the board makes room for it.

Sphere of Safety, Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and other attack taxes show what they cost on the card ("⚔ {2} each"), and the declare-attackers bar shows the tax per attacker and the total for the creatures you've picked.

title: A tidier battlefield
notes: New Organized board layout (the default): both battlefields are laid out in rows — creatures facing each other in the middle, then other permanents, then lands at the back.
Identical permanents stack into one card with a ×N badge: tokens, lands, duplicate creatures and rocks. Tapped and untapped ones stack separately; clicking a stack uses one card from it.
Auras and Equipment tuck behind the permanent they're attached to instead of taking their own spot. Hover one to see it.
Rows shrink their cards to fit the screen before wrapping, and the whole board scales down when it gets crowded, so nothing falls off the edge.
Planeswalkers that can still use a loyalty ability this turn glow green with a ⚡ badge; once used they show "✓ used" (Oath of Teferi and The Chain Veil count).
Prefer placing your cards yourself? Set Board layout to Free on the start screen or in the ☰ menu — the Tidy button comes back.

title: Aetheric Amplifier
notes: Aetheric Amplifier's {4}, {T} ability now asks which mode you want and doubles the counters (it was left to do by hand). Other activated abilities written as "Choose one." with bullet modes work the same way.
The AI doubles the counters where they help it most — its own planeswalker loyalty or +1/+1 counters — and picks that mode only when there's something worth doubling.

title: Smarter auto-tapping
notes: Auto-pay now searches for the best way to tap instead of grabbing the first land that fits. It never fails to pay a cost that can be paid (like {W}{W}{U} off a Hallowed Fountain, a Plains and an Island).

It taps basics before dual lands and Command Tower-style lands, uses Sol Ring and bounce lands' extra mana, pays colored costs without hurting you from pain lands when it can, and saves Treasures, mana creatures and lands with other abilities for last.
Generic costs are paid with the colors the rest of your hand needs least, so the right colors stay open for your next spell. Mana already floating in your pool is always spent first.
The AI uses the same, smarter payment.

title: Extra turn counter
notes: Extra turns waiting (Ral Zarek, Teferi, Time Warp…) show on that player's panel as "⟳ N extra turns left", and a gold "⟳ Extra turn" tag marks a turn that is itself an extra turn.

title: Bounce lands
notes: Bounce lands (Azorius Chancery, Simic Growth Chamber and the rest) return a land you control to your hand when they enter (you pick; it was left to do by hand), and tap for both of their colors — two mana, not one.
Coral Atoll and the other Visions bounce lands ask you to return an untapped land of the right type, or they're sacrificed.
Lands that tap for two specific mana ({T}: Add {C}{U}, {C}{C}…) make both.
The AI won't play a bounce land as its only land, and returns a tapped basic when it plays one.

title: Signets and mobilize
notes: Signets now work like the real thing: {1}, {T} for two mana. Paying for a spell uses another source for the {1} and gets both colors from the Signet (before, a Signet acted like two free mana of either color). Tapping one by hand spends {1} from your mana pool first.
Arcane Signet and Command Tower-style "any color in your commander's color identity" only make your commanders' colors.

Mobilize checked: the Warriors enter tapped and attacking the same player and are sacrificed at the end step. Fixed: Bone-Cairn Butcher's attacking tokens get deathtouch, Zurgo's Vanguard's power counts your creatures, and Zurgo, Thunder's Decree keeps its Warriors at your end step.
Cards that say "this creature's power is equal to…" (the newer wording) count correctly.

title: Jace deck audit
notes: Went through every card in a Jace superfriends list. Planeswalkers: Jace, Memory Adept (−7), Jace, Reality Sculptor (all three abilities, including the 25-loyalty check), Jace, Architect of Thought (attackers −1/−0, the two-pile split, −8), Jace Reawakened (plot, copy every spell), Jace, Mirror Mage (kicker copy at 1 loyalty, the 0), The Eternal Wanderer (+1 return, −4, only one attacker at a time), Vraska, Betrayal's Sting (−2 Treasure, −9 poison), Rowan Kenrith (+2 forced attacks), Ral Zarek (−7 coin flips), Chandra, Bold Pyromancer (−7), Chandra, Flamecaller (0).

Static effects: Gisela (double damage to opponents, half to you), The Wanderer (no noncombat damage), Propaganda and Sphere of Safety (attack taxes — you're asked to pay, the AI pays or attacks with fewer), Oath of Gideon (+1 loyalty), Oath of Teferi (two loyalty abilities a turn), The Chain Veil (end-step life loss and its extra activation), Sanctum Lurker (planeswalkers survive at 0), Gold-Forged Thopteryx (ward on legendaries), Tomik (one attacker per planeswalker).
Emblems now work and show on the player panel: Elspeth's +2/+2 and flying, Jace, Unraveler of Secrets' counter-the-first-spell, Teferi's instant-speed loyalty.

Also: Windcrag Siege and other Sieges ask Mardu or Jeskai (Mardu doubles attack triggers), Theorist's Sanctum enters untapped if you can behold a Jace, Shark Typhoon makes the right-sized Shark (cast and cycled), Plan for All Outcomes, Deepglow Skate and Aetheric Amplifier (double counters), Kher Keep's Kobolds, Fatehold Charm's bounce mode, Dreadhorde Invasion's lifelink, and damage doublers now apply in combat too.

title: Casual AI, attack targets, craft
notes: New setting: AI style — Casual (default) or Competitive, on the start screen and in the ☰ game menu. Casual keeps blockers home instead of swinging out, only spends removal and instant-speed removal on real threats, only casts board wipes when it's far behind, and lets most of your spells resolve instead of countering them. Competitive is the old behaviour.
Attacking creatures show who they're attacking (⚔ 1 → AI, ⚔ 2 → Garruk); an attacked planeswalker glows purple and an attacked player's panel glows red.

Craft works (The Enigma Jewel and other craft cards): choose the materials from your permanents and graveyard and it returns transformed. Locus of Enlightenment gets the activated abilities of what it was crafted from (once each turn) and copies your non-mana abilities.
The Enigma Jewel's mana can only be spent on activated abilities.
Teferi's Talent: the enchanted planeswalker gets the −12 emblem ability and gains a loyalty counter whenever you draw. Emblems are tracked.
Auras that say "enchanted planeswalker" work.

title: The rest of the Way cards
notes: Way of the Healer: the granted −2 now creates the 2/2 Cadet token (named tokens like Cadet work everywhere, e.g. Hexhaven Battalion).
Way of the Warlord: the granted −4 deals its 2 damage to the player as well as the creature or planeswalker.
Way of the Cryomancer: the granted −3 copies your next instant or sorcery spell that turn.
Checked: Way of the Deathbringer, Wildspeaker, Pyromancer, Necromancer.

title: Assemble the Legion, loyalty triggers
notes: Assemble the Legion makes one hasty Soldier per muster counter (it only ever made one). Other "create a token with … for each …" cards are fixed too.

"Whenever you activate a loyalty ability" triggers work: Way of the Paradox (gain 1 life, extra land drop) and Way of the Mind Sculptor (draws only when the ability removed two or more loyalty counters).
"Whenever you put one or more loyalty counters on a planeswalker" triggers work (Inspired Tethermage), from + abilities and from Empower Jace.

title: Way of the … enchantments
notes: "Planeswalkers you control have …" abilities (Way of the Pyromancer, Wildspeaker, Healer, Deathbringer, Warlord, Cryomancer and others) now show up on every planeswalker you control, including the Jace token, and the AI can use them too.

title: Attack highlights, equipment, ghost cards
notes: Declare attackers: creatures that can attack glow gold (summoning-sick, tapped and defender creatures don't).
Steel Overseer only puts counters on artifact creatures (it hit every creature). The same fix applies to every "artifact creature", "enchantment creature" etc. filter.
Adaptive Omnitool, Lashwrithe and other "equipped/enchanted creature gets +1/+1 for each …" now update as the count changes (they were fixed at the moment of attaching).
Fixed leftover "ghost" cards from dragging: if a drag is interrupted (released over a dialog, outside the window, alt-tab), the floating copy is cleaned up.
Checked and working: Terror of Mount Velus, living weapon (Batterskull, Skinwing, Lashwrithe), Adaptive Omnitool's attack trigger.

title: Sagas, per-player turn counter, card sweep
notes: Turn counter: each player's turns are counted separately. The top bar shows the current player's turn number (hover it for both), and the log and the YOUR TURN banner use it too.

Sagas: The Eldest Reborn's chapter III, Urza's Saga (gains its mana and Construct abilities, finds a {0}/{1} artifact), The Akroan War (the stolen creature goes back when the saga leaves, creatures must attack, tapped creatures damage themselves) and Elspeth Conquers Death (cost increase, counter on the returned card) now work.
"Gain control of … for as long as …" effects end when the source leaves the battlefield.

Card sweep over every sample and precon card (about 1,600 cards): fixed Avenger of Zendikar and other "create a token for each …" cards, Chaos Warp, Blink, Living Death, Teferi's Protection, Silence, Plaguecrafter, Goblin Dark-Dwellers, Soul of Windgrace, Puppeteer Clique, Mortuary Mire, Noxious Revival, Chittering Witch, Dire Fleet Ravager, Secret Rendezvous, Ox Drover, Smothering Tithe, Sheoldred, the Apocalypse and Sanguine Bond.

title: Maelstrom Wanderer, Exotic Orchard, pain lands
notes: Maelstrom Wanderer cascades twice (it only cascaded once).
Exotic Orchard and Fellwar Stone only make colors your opponent's lands could make, and Reflecting Pool only what your own lands could make (they made any color before).

Pain lands (Battlefield Forge and friends), Talismans, horizon lands and Mana Confluence cost 1 life when they make colored mana. Paying for spells uses their painless colorless mana first when it can, and the log shows the life paid.
Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm: copies of legendary Dragons now show as nonlegendary on the card.
Checked: Repurposed Enforcer's Empower Jace X works (fixed in 1.2.13).

title: Spellbound Dragon
notes: Spellbound Dragon gets +X/+0 equal to the mana value of the card you actually discarded (it always got +0 before). Other "where X is the discarded card's mana value" effects are fixed too.

title: Bontu, Rakdos Charm, Empower Jace, Curiosity
notes: God-Eternal Bontu: sacrifice any number of other permanents, then draw that many (it drew nothing before). When it dies or is exiled it goes third from the top of your library, not on top.

Rakdos Charm: "exile all cards from target player's graveyard" exiles the whole graveyard, and "each creature deals 1 damage to its controller" works. The AI now picks the mode that fits the board instead of always destroying an artifact; the same smarter mode choice applies to every modal spell.
Empower Jace: puts loyalty counters on your Jace token, creating the blue Jace planeswalker token (−1: Surveil 1, −3: Draw a card) first if you don't have one.

Jace, Multiverse Architect: its combat trigger asks the opponent to pay {2} or be unable to attack your Jaces that turn; the −3 reveals until a creature or planeswalker and puts it onto the battlefield, the rest on the bottom.
"Reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a … card" effects now work in general.
Curiosity, Ophidian Eye, Sigil of Sleep and other "whenever enchanted/equipped creature deals damage to an opponent" auras trigger, including on noncombat damage.
Checked: Amass works (creates the Army or grows the one you have).

title: Maximum hand size
notes: At the end of your turn, if you have more cards than your maximum hand size, you're asked which ones to discard (before, the game only mentioned it in the log).

Maximum hand size changes are counted for both players: Reliquary Tower, Thought Vessel and other "no maximum hand size" cards, "your maximum hand size is increased/reduced by N", and opponents' effects like Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur.

title: Spacecraft and a bigger turn banner
notes: Spacecraft: abilities under STATION 2+, 8+ etc. are only available once the ship has that many charge counters, whichever way the card text is written, and the ship becomes an artifact creature at its last threshold ("It's an artifact creature at 8+"), so it can attack.
A big "YOUR TURN" banner now fills the middle of the screen when your turn starts.

title: War Room
notes: War Room's draw ability now charges life equal to the number of colors in your commanders' color identity (it was free before).

title: AI uses X loyalty abilities
notes: The AI now uses planeswalker abilities with X in the cost. It picks X to match the job: exactly enough damage to kill your best creature it can reach (Chandra Nalaar, Sorin, Grim Nemesis, Chandra, Awakened Inferno), the X that wipes the most of your board for "each creature" effects, or as many tokens or counters as it can while keeping the planeswalker alive (Kasmina, Tibalt).

title: Giada, multi-token spells, planeswalker AI
notes: Giada, Font of Hope: each other Angel enters with a +1/+1 counter for each Angel you already control (it only ever gave one), and Giada's mana can only be spent on Angel spells.
Cards that make several different tokens at once (Trostani's Summoner and friends) now make all of them, not just the first.
Nissa, Who Shakes the World's +1 (and similar effects) turns the land into a creature.
Planeswalker AI: it weighs whether your creatures could kill its planeswalker and goes up in loyalty when it's in danger, instead of spending it down.
Checked and working: Verdant Sun's Avatar, Trostani, Selesnya's Voice, Trostani Discordant.

title: AI crewing
notes: Fixed: the AI tapped every creature it had to crew a vehicle, then attacked with almost nothing. It now taps only the creatures it needs, using ones that can't attack well (summoning sick, low value) first.
The AI no longer crews a vehicle that came in this turn and can't attack yet.

title: Ilysian Caryatid
notes: Ilysian Caryatid taps for two mana of one color while you control a creature with power 4 or greater (it only ever made one before).

title: Unnatural Growth and Ghalta
notes: Unnatural Growth doubles the power and toughness of each creature you control at the beginning of each combat. Other "double the power (and toughness) of …" cards work too.

Ghalta, Primal Hunger costs {X} less where X is the total power of your creatures (from your hand or the command zone). Other "total power" and "greatest power among creatures you control" amounts are counted too.

title: Floating mana
notes: Click an untapped land, mana rock or mana creature to tap it for mana: the mana goes into your pool (shown under your life total) and is spent first when you cast or activate something. Sources that make more than one color ask which color.
Clicked the wrong land? Click it again in the same step to untap it and take its mana back out of the pool.
Treasures and other sacrifice-for-mana sources are sacrificed when you tap them this way.
Mana still floating when the step ends empties from your pool, and the log tells you.

title: Dragonstorm Globe, Endless Ranks, Hit the Mother Lode
notes: Dragonstorm Globe: Dragons you control enter with an extra +1/+1 counter. The same fix covers Grumgully, the Generous, Metallic Mimic and other "each … you control enters with an additional +1/+1 counter" cards.
Endless Ranks of the Dead: makes half as many Zombies as you control, rounded down (it made none before). Other "where X is half …" cards work too.
Hit the Mother Lode: creates tapped Treasures equal to the difference after discovering.

title: Rituals, chosen creature types, a choosier AI
notes: Rituals: Mana Geyser, Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Songs of the Damned, Rite of Flame, Irencrag Feat, Manamorphose, Mana Seism, Cabal Ritual's threshold and Jeska's Will now add the right amount of mana.
Mana permanents that tap for "one mana for each…" now count properly: Gaea's Cradle, Priest of Titania, Elvish Archdruid, Cabal Coffers. Black Lotus taps for three.

Herald's Horn, Vanquisher's Banner and other "As this enters, choose a creature type" cards ask you for a type (the AI picks its deck's most common one) and then work: cost reduction, anthem, card draw and Herald's Horn's upkeep reveal.

Smarter AI: it no longer casts spells whose targets don't exist (reanimating an empty graveyard, removal with nothing to hit), and it saves removal and burn for real threats instead of firing it at tokens, unless it's under pressure.
Chaos Warp and other "shuffle it into its owner's library" spells count as removal for the AI.

title: Patch notes and twelve more precons
notes: New: this patch notes window. It opens after the app updates itself; click the version number on the start screen to see it again.

Twelve new precons: Eternal Might, Squirreled Away, Graveyard Overdrive, Desert Bloom, Most Wanted, Deadly Disguise, Masters of Evil (Doctor Who), Virtue and Valor, Food and Fellowship, Growing Threat, Party Time and Buckle Up.

Fixed commanders: Yuma (Desert cards make Plants), Disa (Lhurgoyfs come back), Brimaz, Blight of Oreskos (proliferate after a Phyrexian dies), Davros (Dalek and villainous choice), Hazel of the Rootbloom (Squirrels copied twice), Kaust, Ellivere, Nalia de'Arnise (full party), Frodo (Ring-bearer draw).
Also fixed: "whenever a … card is put into your graveyard from anywhere" triggers (The Gitrog Monster, Centaur Vinecrasher, Titania).
Triggers whose condition isn't met no longer ask you to apply them by hand.

title: Mardu Surge, tokens that enter attacking
notes: New precon: Mardu Surge (Zurgo Stormrender).
Adeline, Hero of Bladehold, Zurgo and every mobilize card now create their tokens tapped and attacking.
Zurgo Stormrender's token trigger works: draw if the token was attacking, otherwise each opponent loses 1 life.
"Do X if … Otherwise, do Y" now checks the condition instead of doing both.

title: TMNT and World Shaper precons
notes: New precons: Turtle Power! (Leonardo, the Balance) and World Shaper (Hearthhull, the Worldseed).
Partner—Character select commanders can be paired with each other.
Fixed: Korvold's counter-and-draw, Mayhem Devil, Mazirek, Szarel, Splinter, Rat King, Heroes in a Half Shell, April O'Neil, Ray Fillet, Casey Jones, Omnath, God-Eternal Bontu.

title: Space Beleren
notes: Space sculptor works: creatures get alpha, beta or gamma sectors (shown as α β γ), and all three of Space Beleren's abilities work.

title: Foundations Commander precons
notes: The Precon tab has the five Foundations Commander decks.

title: Second screen
notes: Pop the AI's board out into its own window with the ⧉ Pop out button (desktop app 1.1.0 or newer).
Fixed: Otherworldly Journey, Eerie Interlude, Semester's End, Ghostway and other end-step returns; Oubliette; Teferi, Master of Time.

title: More sample decks
notes: Six new sample decks at Bracket 1, Bracket 4 and cEDH, grouped by bracket.
New Precon tab.

title: Blink effects
notes: Fixed: Cloudshift, Ephemerate, Brago, Oblivion Ring, Journey to Nowhere, Fiend Hunter, Detention Sphere; the AI picks sensible flicker targets.

title: Dragonstorms
notes: The Dragonstorm enchantments return to your hand when a Dragon you control enters.

title: Changelings
notes: Changelings such as Firdoch Core count as every creature type, so The Ur-Dragon and other Dragon cost reducers apply to them.

title: First update
notes: Fixed: Sunbird's Invocation, Faeburrow Elder, Archnemesis and a crash on some attack triggers.
